status_summary: On 2025-05-21 CMS announced it would audit every eligible Medicare Advantage contract in each payment year, finish remaining audits for payment years 2018 to 2024 by early 2026, and use samples of 35 to 200 records per contract. On 2025-09-25 the Northern District of Texas, in Humana Inc. v. Becerra (No. 4:23-cv-00909-O, ECF 76 and 77), granted summary judgment on a notice-and-comment claim and vacated and remanded the 2023 RADV final rule as a whole, without reaching the other claims; the government filed a notice of appeal to the Fifth Circuit on 2025-11-21. A CMS memo of 2026-01-27 says HHS will comply with the order while it stands and expects to begin payment year 2020 audits by February 2026. The Fifth Circuit heard argument on 2026-10-05 and no decision was found.

title: Restore Medicare Advantage risk adjustment data validation (RADV) audits
uncertainties: The district court order (ECF 76) and final judgment (ECF 77) were read through a copy hosted by the Georgetown Law litigation tracker, which shows the caption, document numbers and filing header but no typed judge name or signature; the order vacates the 2023 rule as a whole on logical-outgrowth grounds and does not hold extrapolation unlawful. The appellate docket was not opened; the appeal rests on law-firm and news summaries, which agree on a 2025-11-21 notice of appeal (the 2025-11-01 date in one lead was not supported), and the 2026-10-05 Fifth Circuit argument rests on a STAT report. The CMS memo was read as a copy hosted by a trade association. The document calls the RADV rule a Trump-era rule, while the vacated rule was finalized in 2023 from a 2018 proposal. MCIT, MAQI and ACO REACH are not assessed here. Whether payment year 2020 audits began on schedule was not confirmed.
